children: Wall Street's major averages closed deep in the red, taking home weekly loses, as investors sell off technology stocks after a week of discouraging earnings reports.
The benchmark S&P 500 declined 1.82%, while the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite slipped 2.86%. The blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average also fell 1.09%.
On the other hand, the S&P 500 Health Care Sector Index
gained 3.08% for the week.
The top S&P 500 healthcare gainers and losers for the past week are as follows:
Top five gainers:
Regeneron Pharmaceuticals
Eli Lilly
Moderna
Labcorp
Gilead Sciences
Top five losers:
Illumina
Baxter International
ResMed
Boston Scientific
Universal Health Services
Here are some of the important healthcare stories from this week:
Eli Lilly lifts sales outlook as blockbuster weight-loss drugs fuel growth
Eli Lilly
better-than-expected third-quarter results and raised its full-year 2026 revenue outlook, driven by strong demand for Mounjaro and Zepbound.
Indiana-based Lilly
reported non-GAAP earnings of $7.48 per share (+7%),
by $0.87. Revenue surged 38.6% year over year to $24.4B, topping consensus by $1.78B.

Third-quarter revenue growth was driven primarily by Mounjaro and Zepbound. Worldwide sales of Mounjaro, Lilly’s diabetes drug, increased 65% to $10.7B, while its weight-loss treatment Zepbound generated $5.35B. Both drugs outperformed analyst estimates.

The company raised the midpoint of its full-year 2026 revenue guidance by $5.5B, now projecting sales of $91B to $92B, compared to its previous outlook of $85B to $87B and well above analysts’ consensus estimate of $88.74B.
In another news of note, effective Jan. 1, 2027, Eli Lilly will combine its US and international businesses to become Lilly Global Markets.
Merck stock rises as Q3 earnings beat estimates, 2026 outlook raised
Merck
third-quarter results that beat Wall Street expectations and raised its full-year 2026 profit outlook, fueled by stronger sales of cancer blockbuster Keytruda and newer medicines.
The New Jersey-based drugmaker reported non-GAAP earnings of $2.49 per share, beating estimates by $0.40. Revenue rose 4.6% year over year to $18.09B, topping consensus by $760M.

Merck narrowed and raised the midpoint of its full-year 2026 worldwide sales outlook, projecting revenue of $66.8B to $67.3B, compared with the prior forecast of $66.3B-$67.3B and the consensus of $67.04B.

The company also raised and narrowed its full-year non-GAAP earnings forecast to $2.77 to $2.82 per share, versus $2.66-$2.76 previously expected and analysts’ expectations of $2.65. The outlook includes a one-time charge of $0.12 per share related to a global license agreement with SciBrunch.
Surgery Partners to be acquired by Bon Secours for $5.7B
Surgery Partners
will be acquired by HealthSpan Partners, a contractual affiliate of Bon Secours Mercy Health, in an all-cash deal valuing the surgical services provider at $5.7B.
The Financial Times reported earlier that Surgery Partners was in talks to sell a majority stake to Bon Secours.
Under the terms of the agreement, Surgery Partners shareholders, other than affiliates of Bain Capital Private Equity, will receive $23.50 in cash per share.

In connection with the agreement, Bain Capital entered into a voting and support agreement pursuant to which it agreed to vote all of its Surgery Partners shares in favor of the transaction and govern the rollover of its existing equity interests in Surgery Partners at closing.
Bain Capital is currently the largest shareholder of Surgery Partners, collectively owning around 39% of its outstanding shares.
The transaction is expected to close in the first quarter of 2027.

Upon closing of the transaction, Surgery Partners’ operations, including its name, brand, and headquarters, are expected to remain in place. Its common stock will no longer be publicly listed on the Nasdaq Stock Exchange, and Surgery Partners will become a privately held company.
AstraZeneca Q3 profit beats estimates as cancer drug sales drive growth
AstraZeneca
shares rose on Friday after the British drugmaker reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter earnings, driven by robust growth in its oncology business.
Core earnings per share came in at $2.79 (+19% at a constant exchange rate), beating the $2.62 estimated by analysts polled by Bloomberg. Total revenue increased 7% year-over-year to $16.21B.

The company reaffirmed its full-year 2026 guidance, expecting total revenue to increase by a mid-to-high single-digit percentage and core EPS to grow by a low double-digit percentage at constant exchange rates.
Separately, AstraZeneca announced a three-year cost-savings program aimed at generating $1.5B in annual pretax savings, which will primarily be reinvested in its drug development pipeline.
Bayer wins first Roundup trial after Supreme Court ruling
Bayer
won a trial over claims that its Roundup weedkiller caused cancer in three women, its first such victory since the Supreme Court ruled in the company's favor back in June.
The women sued Bayer's
unit Monsanto in 2020, alleging that their regular use of Roundup caused them to develop non-Hodgkin lymphoma. A Missouri jury unanimously ruled in favor of Bayer on Thursday.

"This verdict should send a strong signal that plaintiffs who wish to pursue claims in the court system following the Durnell ruling will face significant challenges both in demonstrating they have viable claims and putting forth the necessary evidence to prove them in ​court," said Bill Dodero, Bayer's
U.S. general counsel and global head of litigation.
In the Durnell ruling, the Supreme Court stated Bayer
could not be sued for failing to warn users about Roundup's cancer risks as federal authorities did not require a warning label for the weedkiller.
This is because the Environmental Protection Agency did not classify glyphosate, a key ingredient in Roundup, as a carcinogen.
Separately, Bayer
has proposed a $7.25B settlement to resolve tens of thousands of other ​lawsuits related to Roundup. This is currently under review by a Missouri state court judge.
